core.q1.q: Is each case different enough that fixed “if this, then that” rules cannot handle it?
core.q1.whyShort: AI only helps when a job needs judgement. If fixed rules can do the job, ordinary software is cheaper and more reliable.
core.q1.guard: Think about the job itself, not how you do it today. If you use rules now only because nothing better existed (for example price rules), answer Not sure.
core.q2.yesIf: It happens often or costs a lot, for example many cases a week, or many staff hours or much revenue involved.
core.q3.whyShort: AI works from your data. If the data is missing or out of date, the tool gives wrong answers that sound sure.
core.q4.yesIf: A person can check the result before it is used, or a mistake is easy to put right.
core.q4.whyShort: AI sometimes makes mistakes, so you need a way to catch them before they hurt anyone.
core.q5.q: Do you know which KPI should improve, and what it is today?
core.m2.why: AI keeps costing money after launch: the subscription, fees based on use, connecting it to your systems, training, and staff time to check results.
core.m3.q: Has the person who approves spending agreed the number (KPI) this tool must improve, with today’s figure and the target?
core.m3.good: The number (KPI), today’s figure and the target, approved in writing and dated.
core.m4.q: Can new AI tools easily be plugged in to your existing infrastructure?
core.m4.good: For each system you want to connect, its provider has confirmed that other software can connect to the version you use.
core.m6.why: AI is never right every time. Someone must be able to catch a wrong result and put it right before it is used.
core.m6.good: A named role that checks the results, knows which results must be checked before they are used, and can stop or correct the tool.
core.m7.name: Data you can reach and keep correct
core.m7.q: Is each piece of data this tool needs held in a system, with a named person who keeps it correct?
core.m7.why: AI works from your data. If the facts are on paper, out of date or spread over systems that disagree, the tool gives wrong answers that sound sure.
core.m8.q: Have the staff involved been told about the plan, and do they know who to tell when the tool gets something wrong?
core.m8.good: The staff involved have heard the plan from their manager, and one named person collects what goes wrong.
core.m10.good: A short written backup plan for each task the tool does, which the shift leaders know.
